At the trial she stood up and yelled that her father was not dead, which was TRUE, and then somebody shot the JUDGE.

*"Seems like her coverup worked, wahaha."*

He LAUGHED. Waluigi wants to be furious about that and Waluigi cannot quite manage it, because Waluigi has watched a tape of two brothers destroying each other SIX TIMES in a dark room and laughing is one of only two available options.

One more thing and then Waluigi will stop. She got up in COURT and insisted, on the record, that her father was not dead. She was RIGHT. She was the only person in that entire room telling the TRUTH, she was doing it against her own interest, and she was held in CONTEMPT for it.

Waluigi thinks about that more than Waluigi would like. **Being right is not a defence.** Waluigi has built an entire career on the assumption that it is.

He made the calls from a COMPANY LINE. Waluigi needs everyone to sit with that. The Wario Files exist as evidence in the public record of this continent because the man committing them did it on a phone that helpfully wrote everything down for him, and when Waluigi pointed this out he SHRUGGED. He shrugged! *It worked, didn't it.*

A debt, then a favour, then a threat. In that order. Escalating POLITELY. He remembers what each one cost to the exact coin, years later, no ledger, no notes, while Waluigi cannot reliably remember whether Waluigi has eaten. There is a kind of monstrousness that is really just extremely good bookkeeping, and Waluigi is looking directly at it across a kitchen table.

And he was not ASHAMED. That is the thing. He did not tell it as a scandal he survived, he told it as a PROCEDURE THAT WORKED, with a little pride in the sequencing, and Waluigi wrote the whole list down and has not put the pencil down since. **Waluigi picked up a pencil.** For the first time in two days. Because of THAT story.

sections.heading: He Went Through Waluigi's Room Like A VAULT And Found The Worst Thing In It
sections.body:
Later he came back in and went over the room PROPERLY. Not snooping - Waluigi knows snooping, Waluigi INVENTED snooping - this was a man appraising a vault. Wario has one genuine talent and it is knowing which object in a room is the valuable one.

What is on Waluigi's walls: newspaper clippings. Tournament results, years of them, and on every single one Waluigi's own name circled where it appears. Waluigi is aware of how that looks. Waluigi does not require commentary on how that looks.

What is on Waluigi's desk: cold spaghetti and a stack of handwritten letters, crumpled, **none of them sent.**

He picked one up between two fingers and read it. *"I know you probably don't care about any of this but I had to say something before I lost my mind."*

And then - and Waluigi watched him do this - he folded it and put it back **EXACTLY WHERE HE FOUND IT.**

Wario does not put things back. Wario has never put anything back in his LIFE. Wario once took a chandelier. Waluigi has seen this man pocket cutlery in a house where somebody had just DIED. And he put the letter back in its place like it was hot.

Then he backed toward the door without a word, got caught, turned around, and said: *"Your handwriting's terrible."*

**IT IS FINE.** Waluigi's handwriting is FINE. It is a FAST hand. It is the handwriting of somebody who is WRITING SOMETHING DOWN rather than PERFORMING, which Waluigi would have thought a former head of state might RECOGNISE.

The letters are not addressed to anybody. Waluigi is not going to explain that in a commentary and Waluigi would ask the reader to notice that Wario did not ask either.

Drawers out. Wardrobe onto the bed. The loose board by the radiator found in UNDER A MINUTE, which tells the reader everything about how this man has spent his professional life. Eleven letters nobody was ever going to receive. Clippings folded to the same column for years, with one name pressed into the paper hard enough to emboss the sheet behind it.

Waluigi sat in the chair and LET HIM. That is not nothing. Waluigi has thrown people out of this room for looking at the desk. Waluigi watched a man empty a wardrobe onto a bed and said nothing, because saying something would have required admitting there was something in there worth protecting.

He got to the bottom of the box. He looked at the thing at the bottom of the box for a long time. And then he put it back FACE DOWN, exactly as he found it, and stood up and insulted the handwriting on a letter he had already read.

**He has still not mentioned it.** Not a hint, not a leverage play, not one cheap shot in an argument where it would have won him the argument instantly. Waluigi keeps waiting for the invoice. Waluigi is starting to suspect there is not going to be one, and does not know what to do with a world that works like that.

sections.heading: And Then WARIO Solved It. Wario. WARIO.
sections.body:
Waluigi told him he had learned nothing from the tapes. Waluigi was showing off. Waluigi was being CRUEL, frankly, because Luigi is in a hospital bed and Waluigi wanted somebody else to feel bad too.

And Wario just **smiled** and said: Luigi is still in hospital, you locked yourself in your room and learned nothing from these tapes, but you know what *I* learned.

Then he explained it, and Waluigi's stomach went through the FLOOR.

Everyone has been reading the courier's note like a rescue. *The star is not lost. Find the garden above the fire.* Heroic. Noble. Mario hiding to protect something, leaving a trail for the good guys.

Wario said: **run it as GREED.**

And the whole sentence TURNS OVER. *The star is not lost* is not reassurance. It is an **INVENTORY LINE**. The star is not lost because nobody took it and nobody destroyed it. It is not lost because somebody still HAS it. And if Mario went east after the fountain and has stayed gone this long, then *the garden above the fire* is not where he was taken to.

**It is where he is KEEPING it.**

Waluigi said *"greed, of course that's your angle"* and then Waluigi did not look away, because Waluigi already had the pencil out.

Waluigi believes him. Waluigi has written that sentence three times tonight and deleted it twice. **For once in Waluigi's miserable life Waluigi believes someone who isn't Waluigi,** and that should terrify Waluigi considerably more than it does.

How many people have died because nobody asked the right question until a disgraced dead man in a basement pointed his finger and LAUGHED?

Waluigi hates that it makes sense. **WAH.**

*The star is not lost.* Everyone in this archive, Waluigi INCLUDED, read that as comfort. As a stranger being kind on paper. Because that is how you read a sentence when you are hoping, and everybody involved in this arc has been hoping so hard for so long that nobody checked the grammar.

Wario read it as a STATUS LINE. An inventory note. The sentence you write when the item is still on the books and still where you left it, and the only reason to write it down at all is that somebody PAID to have it put there and wants confirmation the arrangement held.

Waluigi spent six minutes trying to break it. Six. Waluigi has broken better theories than this in under thirty seconds, from across a room, while eating. There is no hole in it. *Not lost* is not hope, it is a RECEIPT. *The garden above the fire* is not a riddle, it is an ADDRESS. The star is not lost because somebody HAS it, and is keeping it somewhere warm and high and very difficult to walk into.

So the working theory of this entire arc now belongs to a man who once faked his own death to avoid a go-kart race, and Waluigi has filed it in Waluigi's OWN HANDWRITING, under protest, and the handwriting is FINE.

sections.heading: And Then Waluigi Typed Out The Whole Thing. Every Word. Including The Ones That Hurt.
sections.body:
One more section and then Waluigi will let the reader go.

The whole tape is now in the archive. All of it. Typed out by hand, in order, with the stumbles left in and the bad grammar left in and Mario's ridiculous accent left in, because CLEANING IT UP IS ALREADY AN EDIT and this archive has had quite enough of those.

Do you know how long that took? Waluigi does. Waluigi was there. Ninety seconds of tape, and Waluigi stopped and started it so many times that the machine started making a noise it should not make.

**And here is the part that Waluigi would like on the record.** Waluigi could have summarised it. Waluigi is GOOD at summarising. Waluigi could have given the archive eight tidy paragraphs saying what the argument meant, and every single reader would have taken Waluigi's word for it, because that is what readers DO, and because until this week nobody in this entire organisation had anything better than the recollection of a man who was **not in the room and was wearing somebody else's face at the time.**

Instead Waluigi filed the thing itself. Which means any idiot with a search bar can now go and check Waluigi's reading against the source and find out that Waluigi got something wrong. Somebody WILL. Waluigi has made a rod for Waluigi's own back and did it deliberately and is furious about it.

Because here is the alternative, and Waluigi wants everyone to look at it clearly. An archive that only files the sources which happen to flatter its archivist is not an archive. **It is a SCRAPBOOK.** It is a man with a glue stick deciding what the past was.

There are two things in that transcript Waluigi would genuinely rather nobody read. Waluigi is not going to say which two. They are in there. They are in there with everything else and they are in there in full and the reason is that the moment Waluigi starts taking things out, Waluigi becomes the fourth person to edit this tape, and Waluigi has spent this entire filing complaining about the other three.

**WAH.** Go and read it. Check Waluigi's work. Waluigi has never meant anything less and has never been more certain it was correct.

One last thing. Waluigi reread the transcript after typing it and found something that was not audible when it was only SOUND. On the page, the two of them keep finishing in the same place. Same rhythm, same beat, same number of syllables, over and over, for ninety seconds - two men who cannot agree on a single fact and who are nevertheless perfectly in time with each other the entire way down.

**They were still a duo. Right to the last word. Neither of them noticed.**

commentaries.title: Judgement in the Grove
commentaries.subtitle: Waluigi's Cut — a musket reloaded in the open, the Iron Legion calling pest control, a robot dog committing assault as first aid, and one kneeling man
commentaries.filed: 3 Aethel, 1040 BF — two days after the grove, from a desk, by someone who was not there
commentaries.pullQuote: PEST CONTROL. A professional soldier, in armour, inside a hostile pocket dimension, requesting an exterminator. There is no exterminator. There is no telephone. There is no sky.
commentaries.standfirst: Everything that happened in the Skittering Grove after the rope, told properly, loudly, by someone who was not in it. Contains: an arrow put back in a pocket, a toad standing in front of a centaur, a recruitment pitch involving a tree of love, two parties who cannot agree what building they are in, and an execution the archive declines to call either murder or justice.

sections.heading: Waluigi Was Not There, Which Is The Only Reason Waluigi Is Still Funny
sections.body:
Waluigi was not in that grove. Waluigi wants that at the top, in writing, before a single joke, because this filing ends with a man on his knees and Waluigi is about to be extremely loud for three thousand words on the way there.

Here is how it opens. Remi says "it's a little smoky in here" and walks back the way she thinks she came, which in a grove with no sky is a SENTENCE WITH NO MEANING. There is no back. There is no way she came. She gets turned around in the smoke and walks directly into the spiders. Waluigi has read a lot of filings that begin with a plan. This one begins with a girl getting lost indoors.

And then she does the best thing anybody does all night, and Waluigi needs the reader to slow down for it, because it will be buried under a scythe in about ninety seconds.

She draws a crossbow arrow. She looks at the ettercap. AND SHE PUTS THE ARROW BACK IN HER POCKET. Back in the pocket. She takes out the musket instead, and she hits it, directly, first shot.

Waluigi wants to explain why that is the single most professional act in this entire document. A crossbow is fast. A musket is not. A musket is a decision you have to live inside for a very long time afterwards, and she took it in the middle of a smoke bank with spiders already moving. She did the arithmetic and she took the SLOW LOUD OPTION because the slow loud option was the one that would actually land.

Then she reloads it. Slowly. In the open. The record says — and Waluigi loves this line, Waluigi would like it carved above the door — "they stand there." Everybody just STANDS THERE while the fourteen-year-old works a ramrod down a barrel in front of a hostile brood. And then she hits it again.

Two direct hits. In smoke. With a reload in the open in between. Waluigi has personally watched grown adventurers with better equipment and worse manners fail to do that twice in a career.

Meanwhile the Scorncrow is having a conversation. "You invaded my home, right?" it says, which Waluigi initially filed as villain patter and now has to sit with, because of what it says twenty minutes later about a treehouse. Markop asks the practical question — will the spiders attack — and the thing answers him honestly. "They'll come around." It is not bluffing. It is giving him a weather report. WAH. Nobody adjusts.

And Waluigi wants one more thing on the record before the scythe comes out, because it will be impossible to say gracefully afterwards. Everything in this opening is somebody making a small correct decision inside a situation that is already lost. Remi trades speed for accuracy. Markop asks for a threat assessment instead of charging. Those are GOOD INSTINCTS. Waluigi has spent multiple filings complaining that this party plans like a bar fight, and here they are, in the dark, with no exit and no sky, quietly doing it properly.

It does not help even slightly. Waluigi wants the reader to carry that forward into every remaining section, because the temptation at the end of this filing is going to be to say they got what was coming to them. They did not. THEY PLAYED IT WELL AND THE GROVE DID NOT CARE, and those are two separate facts, and Waluigi is going to keep them separate no matter how badly the last page wants to merge them.

sections.heading: The Scythe Grazes Three People And The Iron Legion Calls Pest Control
sections.body:
The Scorncrow hurls the scythe. Waluigi is quoting the record directly here because the record earned it: its spinning form shrouded in powerful magic, cleaving everything in its path, CHILLING COLD CUTTING THROUGH ANYONE CAUGHT IN THE WAKE.

It hits Eager. It hits Archie. It hits Dan. Three people on one line.

And it grazes all three. Waluigi wants the reader to hold those two facts next to each other, because a weapon that cleaves everything in its path hit three separate bodies and killed none of them. Either this party is the luckiest collection of idiots in the Shadowfell, or that throw was never meant to kill anybody. Waluigi is not going to tell you which. Waluigi is merely observing that the thing spent its biggest swing on a line that inconvenienced three people and removed none, and that a tactician who opened the LAST session by deleting the healer first does not usually miss by accident.

Then a spider goes for Eager, Markop hits it back, and Markop — the record is very clear — goes THUMP THUMP. A giant green spider goes thump thump toward the Iron Legion guards. Waluigi has read this passage six times and Waluigi is confident the archive is meant to hear hooves and legs at the same time, in the dark, closing.

Remi gets webbed. She is damaged and clawed at and her clothes are ripped and she yells "WHY. WHYYYY." Waluigi has nothing clever for that. That is just a child getting hurt in the dark and asking the only question available.

And the Iron Legion — the IRON LEGION, the standing military apparatus of this continent, the organisation that has spent multiple filings arresting Waluigi's colleagues on procedural grounds — looks at the spiders and says:

> "We gotta call pest control. RETREAT!"

PEST CONTROL. Waluigi is going to be annoyed about this for the rest of Waluigi's life and Waluigi is ALSO never going to let it go. That is a professional soldier, in armour, inside a hostile pocket dimension, requesting an exterminator. There is no exterminator. There is no telephone. There is no sky. WAH.

And Remi, tied up, with another spider walking toward her, says "come on, I'm looking at my spells" — with the book IN FULL VIEW. Waluigi would like the reader to picture the composition: a webbed teenager openly consulting the manual while something with eight legs approaches, asking the table for a minute. Waluigi has never loved this archive more than in that exact sentence.

sections.heading: Feyward Dan Stands In Front Of Everyone, Including The Centaur
sections.body:
Now Waluigi has to be sincere for a paragraph, and Waluigi resents it.

Feyward Dan stands in front of everyone. The record specifies: INCLUDING MARKOP. Waluigi needs the reader to understand the physical comedy and the actual courage sitting in the same image, because they are inseparable. Markop is an armoured centaur. He is enormous. Feyward Dan is a toad who comes up to roughly the centaur's knee, and he walked past him to be the thing standing closest to the Scorncrow.

Then he gets out a religious symbol STUDDED WITH MUSHROOMS and points it at the brood, and the brood turns. Waluigi has filed a lot of holy symbols. None of them had mushrooms on. This one worked. Waluigi is forced to concede that the mushrooms may not be the decorative part.

Dan moves behind the spider. Dan swings once, Eager sneak attacks, and the spider ROARS. Eager then runs while it is distracted and immediately runs INTO A SPIDERY BUSH, which Waluigi considers the most Eager sequence ever recorded: flawless tactical execution followed instantly by walking into the scenery.

Markop walks past the spider. It bites at him. It misses. He does not even turn around for it — he is already facing the Scorncrow, and the Scorncrow greets him with "oh, you come to offer your head, how vigilant."

Markop says nothing. Waluigi wants that noted, because Markop is not usually a man who says nothing. He STARES. He walks closer. He raises the warhammer, and the hammer glows, and a sky that does not exist opens up anyway and puts thunder into it.

Divine favour. Held since before the rope. Waluigi wants the reader to appreciate the accounting: Markop has been carrying that charge through an entire descent, through a sealed door, through a marching order, waiting for a target worth spending it on. That is not luck. THAT IS A MAN WHO PACKED.

He strikes. The Scorncrow blocks. THE BLOCK DOES NOT HOLD. And the thing flinches — for the first time across four separate engagements, this creature flinches — and then it strikes him in the head and SPLITS HIS SKULL and Markop keeps standing there bleeding while it laughs at him.

And then it says the thing. "I have lived in this tree, made it my treehouse when I was little."

Waluigi is not laughing at that one. Last filing, a musket at point-blank range took the mask off and found human blood underneath, and Waluigi had to publish a correction for having called it a monster three times. This is the second piece of physical evidence in two sessions. It had a childhood. It had a treehouse. Waluigi is keeping the correction in force.

sections.heading: A Recruitment Pitch, An Arrest Warrant, And A Geography Argument
sections.body:
Archie Miser — three-eyed, dimension-hopping, having split between worlds — prepares a FIREBALL. He winds up. He builds it. And then: "nah, just kidding," he winks at nobody in particular, and delivers a firebolt instead.

Waluigi wants to be clear that this is a man performing a bit, to an audience of nobody, in the middle of a fight he is losing, against something that has already split a centaur's head open. Waluigi respects it enormously and thinks it was insane.

The Scorncrow coughs blood and says "I'm still alive," and then makes an offer, and Waluigi needs the reader to actually hear it:

> "Listen — do you think the worst person can change? We can hang people together on the tree of love. Join me, young one. Join the Scorncrow, or hear my last ballad."

THE TREE OF LOVE. Waluigi has read that phrase forty times now and it gets worse every single time, because "hang people together" is doing an enormous amount of work in that sentence and Waluigi cannot tell you which meaning was intended. Neither can the record. The record does not say.

Archie declines: "sorry Scorncrow, I'm on the side of good, despite all my accidental crimes." Waluigi would like ACCIDENTAL CRIMES entered into the permanent legal record as a defence, because Waluigi intends to use it.

The guards retreat deeper into the grove and then — mid-battle, while losing, while surrounded — announce "YOU TOADS ARE UNDER ARREST," spot Archie, and try to serve a warrant. In a spider pit. During a fight. Waluigi has to hand it to the Iron Legion: the paperwork does not stop for anything, including reality.

So they negotiate a temporary alliance, and the terms are that Archie gets arrested at the end. He shrugs. "This won't last." Waluigi agrees with him and files it as the only accurate prediction anybody makes all night.

Then the geography argument happens, and Waluigi would like a moment.

Archie asks what the guards are doing DOWN HERE. The guard says: down here, what do you mean? Archie explains — the rope, the lair, the descent, we are in the undergrowth. Markop offers that the tree is a teleporter. And the guard says:

> "What are you guys talking about? This is the ruined manor."

Waluigi wants everybody to stop and look at that. Two groups of people are standing in the same grove, in the same fight, at the same moment, and they DO NOT AGREE ON WHERE THEY ARE. One party climbed down a rope into a pit. The other party thinks it walked into a manor. Both are correct about their own route. Nobody in that grove knows what the building is doing, and the one man who said "the tree is a teleporter" said it as a throwaway.

Then a punch goes WACHOW, Wario laughs, and announces "I am tired of running." Markop shouts that it has been LIKE SIX SECONDS. Wario clarifies that he is simply a bad runner. Archie yells that this is all Wario's fault, and Wario says "alright then, I'll leave." WAH! Waluigi has been in that exact conversation and Waluigi also threatened to leave.

sections.heading: BARK BARK, And The Man Remi Found Asleep
sections.body:
Salam fires at the ettercap and misses. Dan does it at the same time and misses. Then Feyward Dan swings in tandem with Eager and they BOTH HIT and the ettercap goes down, and everyone turns to the Scorncrow at once. Eager heals himself with DUCT TAPE. Waluigi has no follow-up. The record says duct tape. Waluigi has decided not to investigate the medical theory.

Remi is about to get eaten. A spider comes down to bite her. And then:

> BARK BARK

Mossy — the steel defender, a construct, a machine that barks — rams her side-on at a dead run. She goes flying into the leaves and the branches, falls out the other side, and lands sitting on the floor. Waluigi wants it recorded that the most effective medical intervention in this session was administered by a robot dog at full speed, and that it consisted of ASSAULTING THE PATIENT.

She gets up and runs and runs and she is alone in the woods. Waluigi is going to stay with her for a moment, because what happens next is the strangest thing in the filing and almost nobody was there for it.

She investigates. She finds a dead body. Wait — no. He is BREATHING.

He has a RED PUNCH MARK on his forehead. Waluigi would like to direct the reader's attention to section four of this same document, in which Wario throws an off-screen punch that goes WACHOW at a target the record never identifies. Waluigi is not going to assert that these are the same event. Waluigi is merely going to put them in the same paragraph and step back.

Remi taps his head with a stick. Lightly. Nothing happens.

Mossy runs back to her. And Remi — fourteen years old, alone, armour destroyed, dress torn, having been webbed and clawed and rammed by her own side — tells the steel defender to WAKE THE GUY UP BY STEPPING ON HIM.

The hard steel presses onto the man's ribcage. The steel defender barks and lowers slightly onto his chest. A CRACK IS HEARD.

"Welp," Remi thinks. "I killed a guy in his sleep."

Waluigi is going to drop the voice for four sentences, because the guide says he gets to do that once per filing and Waluigi is spending it here. That is a child who has been hurt repeatedly in the dark for several hours, finding an unconscious stranger and improvising with the only tool she has, which is a dog made of metal. The record does not say the man died. It says a crack was heard and that she thinks she killed him. Nobody has gone back to check, and the archive does not currently know whether Remi Akamatsu is carrying a killing or a very bad bruise.

Then, in the middle of all of that, somebody shouts "we're coming to get you home, Remi" — and she hears the word HOME and it stops her, because of everything in her own file, and she shakes her head and focuses on the mission. Her dress is torn. She needs new armour. She keeps going. Waluigi picks the voice back up now.

sections.heading: The Warhammer Has Spoken, And Waluigi Files It As Neither
sections.body:
Markop swings on the Scorncrow. It blocks with the scythe.

"Wait — please. I will change."

Its head splits open and starts GLOWING. And it says: "wait, please, I am human. I am not a monster."

And then it starts to KNEEL.

"You're a paladin, right? You have to spare me. Please. I will change ways."

The head splits open. The warhammer has spoken and given him judgement. Markop picks up the scythe.

Waluigi is going to be careful now, and the reader is owed an explanation of why.

Three filings ago Waluigi called that thing a monster. Two filings ago Waluigi called it a monster again. Last session a fourteen-year-old put a musket against its face at point-blank range and the mask came off and THE BLOOD UNDERNEATH WAS HUMAN, and Waluigi published a correction and said Waluigi would not call it a monster a fourth time. Waluigi is keeping that promise in the one filing where keeping it is expensive.

So here is the archive's position, stated plainly and once. A man knelt down, said he was human, addressed a paladin by his office, and asked for mercy, and the paladin killed him. Waluigi is NOT calling that murder. The thing had just split that same paladin's skull. It had spent four engagements hunting these people. It had offered, minutes earlier, to hang people on a tree. Anyone who reads the appeal as sincere has not read the previous four filings.

And Waluigi is not calling it justice either. Justice has a procedure and this had a warhammer. Nobody weighed anything. Nobody asked the other eight people in the grove. The appeal was made to a specific office — PALADIN — and the office did not answer it, it simply concluded.

The archive files it as neither, and the archive is going to let that sit there uncomfortably, because Waluigi genuinely does not know and Waluigi is not going to invent a verdict to make the paperwork tidier. Waluigi is a coward about many things and pretending to certainty is not going to be one of them today.

Then Markop PICKS UP THE SCYTHE, which Waluigi notes without comment except to say that a man who has just executed something and then takes its weapon is a man the archive will be watching in the next filing.

And it does not end there, because the grove does not care. Embercap and giant spiders surround the place OUT OF EVERY GROVE, from every direction at once. Markop feels a shadow over him and a blaze of heat off his shoulder as fire goes past him into the ettercap. A guard is killed by a spider. And a spider claws Salam across the face and he falls unconscious and THE RECORD SAYS IT SCARS.

Salam has fallen. He was not recovered. The archive has commissioned a new likeness of him carrying that scar, because this one does not heal clean and pretending otherwise would be a lie told with a picture.

They killed the thing they came for and their position got WORSE. Markop's skull is split. Archie is under arrest by agreement. Remi is alone over a man she may have killed in his sleep. Salam is down and nobody has him. WAH. Waluigi files this as a victory in the same way a building can be described as structurally standing.

commentaries.title: Waluigi's Cut: The Roll Call at Trinity
commentaries.subtitle: Eleven children, one clipboard, and an acronym that got explained by accident
commentaries.pullQuote: She said, in a full classroom, that she is not on any list. Nobody contradicted her. Waluigi has filed that in two places so it cannot be lost.
commentaries.standfirst: A new advisor took Classroom 2-B at Trinity General School, ran a roll call, and answered a question he could have let die in the noise. Waluigi was not in the room and has never been to Kivotos. Waluigi has opinions regardless.

sections.heading: The Man Came In Adjusting Glasses He Does Not Need
sections.body:
Waluigi wants to begin with the glasses, because the glasses are the whole man.

The record says he stepped through the sliding door adjusting a pair of spectacles that he does not require for vision. Not *needs and is vain about.* Not *forgot he was wearing.* The record is specific: he does not need them to see. He wears them anyway, and he touched them on the way in, which means he wanted the room to watch him touch them. Waluigi has been in this business a long time and Waluigi knows a costume when one walks past. The man arrived IN CHARACTER. He arrived, and he said **call me Sensei**, and he described himself as *the glue holding this whole operation together* — which is a strange thing to call yourself on day one of a job where you have met precisely nobody.

Then he spun around once and pointed at nothing in particular. WAH. That is not a criticism, understand. Waluigi has a great deal of professional sympathy for a man who spins and points, because Waluigi also has bits, and Waluigi also deploys them in rooms that have not yet decided whether to respect him. But it does tell you what he thought he was walking into, and what he thought he was walking into was an audience.

What he actually walked into was a JURISDICTION.

They came at him in order, and the order is the whole seating chart. From the window seats, a hand straight up: *does this mean you'll be around to chat during break too?* — which is a child checking, in the first fifteen seconds, whether this adult is the kind who leaves at the bell. From the front row, a formal welcome and the Sisterhood Club's assistance offered before he had asked for anything. Waluigi notes that one girl had already assessed him as someone who would shortly need help.

And then the door opened a second time, because Misono Mika had not finished arriving. She came through roughly ten seconds before the rest of the class had processed that anything was happening, and she did not walk to a desk. She went straight for HIS desk, slammed both palms flat onto it hard enough to set the pencil holder rattling, and demanded to know whether arriving first made her his favourite student.

Waluigi would like to award a medal here. Not for the entrance — the entrance is standard — but for what came next, which is that she sat down in the desk directly opposite his and adopted what the record calls a princess-like posture. Back straight. Hands folded. Chin elevated. She annexed the front of the classroom in under twenty seconds and then sat in it like it had always been hers, and Waluigi has watched grown warlords take three campaigns to accomplish less.

Then she offered him tea she had not brought.

**I didn't bring tea. But I *thought* about bringing tea. …The thought counts.**

Waluigi is obliged to report that the thought does NOT count. Waluigi is also obliged to report that it worked, because he did not correct her, and nobody in that room has corrected her in what sounds like years — a newcomer asked whether this was really the right place and was told, cheerfully, that Mika-senpai does this with every new teacher and you will get used to it, *oh, probably never, actually.* That is an institution describing itself. Mika is WEATHER. You do not object to weather.

And the man, catching the whispering, delivered his first real line of the morning: something about how if they were comparing him to their last advisor who *mysteriously disappeared*, he assured them he is much harder to get rid of.

Waluigi stopped the tape there. Waluigi rewound it. Waluigi played it again.

Nobody laughed. Nobody asked. Eleven children heard a stranger make a joke about the disappearance of the adult who previously stood where he was standing, and not one of them treated it as new information. Waluigi is going to be filing that sentence for a long time. He tapped the desk twice with a knuckle and called roll.

Waluigi will put it plainly. Waluigi has covered intakes at two war colleges, one monastery and a guild of licensed arsonists, and NOT ONE of them opened with a missing-persons joke. Waluigi flags it. Waluigi moves on. Waluigi will be coming back to it.

sections.heading: Eleven Names, Eleven Completely Different Ways Of Having One
sections.body:
A roll call is the cheapest characterisation device in the business and Waluigi has never seen one work this hard.

He went down the clipboard with his finger, efficient, and the class answered, and every single answer was a different species of answer. Kurimura Airi: present, with a wave, enthusiastic. Easy. Next.

Shirasu Azusa: nothing. Silence, and then a tiny voice from the corner mumbling something inaudible, and the advisor said *I'll take that as a yes* and moved on. Waluigi wants the geography of that corner on the record, because the record gives it and the record is right to. Her desk is in the far corner, angled slightly away from the room, as far from every other desk as a desk can get while still being furniture in the same country. Her posture was immaculate. Her pen was aligned exactly parallel to the edge of her notebook. A breeze came through a cracked window and pushed a strand of hair across her face and SHE DID NOT MOVE TO FIX IT. Waluigi has interviewed assassins with less self-control than that fourteen-year-old.

Ibaragi Yoshimi: a sharp intake of breath. That is it. That is her ENTIRE response to her own name — an audible flinch from the middle row, knuckles white on the desk edge, shoulders trying to fold her into a smaller volume. She got out *I'm here.* Then her eyes swept the room to find out who had witnessed it, landed on the advisor looking directly at her, and she flinched again and looked away fast. Waluigi will be blunt: that is not shyness. Shyness does not audit the room afterwards. That is somebody who has learned that being noticed has a COST.

Iochi Mari: a polite nod. Filed.

**…Shaggy.**

Dead silence. Heads turning. The advisor scanning the room and sighing through his nose before announcing that they were either missing Shaggy or he was hiding behind that sleeping kid in the back row. And a hand came up slowly from behind a desk near the window where the man had been crouched — CROUCHED — attempting to become invisible during ROLL CALL. He stood up with his slouch fully deployed, green shirt off one shoulder, and produced *uh… yo. Present. Like, hi.* His voice cracked on *hi.*

Waluigi does not know what this person is doing in Kivotos. Waluigi does not know how he got there or who enrolled him or why a lanky snack enthusiast with a documented dog is registered at an academy on a different plane from everything Waluigi thought he knew about him. Waluigi is choosing, for now, to simply write it down, because the archive has learned the hard way that demanding explanations up front only produces bad ones.

Then the clipboard produced **Lord Verity**, and the advisor squinted at it, looked around for anyone matching that description, found the newcomer sitting right there, arched an eyebrow, said *huh, you're Lord Verity? …Alright then,* and made a confident checkmark.

He was wrong. The correction did not stay quiet.

A chair scraped. A boy stood up. Every head turned. And:

**YES I AM LORD VERITY. AND I SHALL BE YOUR MASTER FROM THIS DAY FORWARD — KNEEL BEFORE ME, MORTALS!**

Stunned silence. A cough. Mika giggling. Airi covering her mouth. And the advisor blinking twice and going back to his clipboard with **…Right. Next.** Waluigi could not have handled it better and Waluigi is a professional.

The rest came fast. Kenzaki Tsurugi did not raise her hand at all — arms crossed, boots up on the desk, hair over one eye, a low *keheh*, and **…What a pain.** Asagao Hanae raised trembling fingers and whispered that she was here, *p-please take care of me,* sleeve over her knuckles, eyes down. Asa Hanko had to prompt him twice before he found the line. And one more student sat near the back watching, not leaning toward anybody, which in that particular room made them the most conspicuous person present.

Eleven names. Four minutes. Waluigi has read war councils with less in them.

And Waluigi wants one structural observation on the record before the next section, because Waluigi suspects it will matter later: the advisor got a name WRONG, assigned it confidently to the wrong child, and only found out because the correct claimant stood up and shouted. He is working from a list he has never checked against faces. Waluigi does not think that is laziness. Waluigi thinks NOBODY briefed him either.

sections.heading: The Adult Shouted Twice And The Girl Asked Once
sections.body:
Here is where the morning got away from him, and Waluigi wants it understood that this section is not about chaos. It is about who holds POWER in a room that has no formal power in it at all.

First the chaos, for completeness. Airi got out of her seat mid-proceedings and walked the aisle to the back with a second chocolate, weaving between desks with what the record calls practiced ease — *practiced*, meaning she does this, meaning this is a route she has taken before — and sat down next to Shaggy. She warned him not to let Sensei see him eating candy during the speech. He unwrapped it, ate it, and slouched lower, as though horizontal displacement were a form of stealth. Then he leaned in at a volume the record specifically flags as NOT REMOTELY QUIET ENOUGH and asked why Lord Verity was acting weird again and whether today was a cosmic alignment. His leg was bouncing hard enough to vibrate the desk.

At the front, the advisor raised his clipboard like a shield and went to volume. **ALRIGHT! SEATS! NOW!**

Nothing. Chairs kept scraping. Mika had, at some point nobody observed, relocated from her chair to the top of her desk. Waluigi wishes to note that she did not do this to defy him; she did it because the desk was there.

So he tried specificity instead of volume — *I don't care who you are or what club you're in, you sit down, you pay attention, and you behave like students. Not… whatever this is* — and his eyes swept a room containing Lord Verity mid-pose, Shaggy half-swallowed by his own hoodie, Azusa staring at a wall, and Mika spinning on her chair for reasons that remain unestablished. From the back, Tsurugi watched with her eyes narrowed to razor slits and pulled out her phone under the desk, thumb hovering, visibly weighing whether this was worth recording. **…What a circus.**

Waluigi notes she did not press record. Waluigi notes she considered it. There is a person in that back row who is building a file, and Waluigi respects a colleague.

Then Lord Verity escalated, because of course he did, slamming both fists down hard enough to rattle every pencil within two feet: **THIS CLASS WILL COME TO ATTENTION OR FACE THE WRATH OF LORD VERITY HIMSELF!** Airi giggled. Mika kept spinning. The back row did not look up. His wrath achieved a total measured effect of ZERO.

And then Iochi Mari stood up.

She did not shout. Waluigi wants that in bold and Waluigi wants it underlined twice on a whiteboard. She walked to the front. She positioned herself slightly behind the advisor's desk — not at it, BEHIND it, which is a spatial decision so deft Waluigi had to sit down for a moment — gave a small nod to the students nearest her, a silent signal, and said, softly:

**If everyone could take their seats properly, that would be wonderful~**

The record: *cutting through the noise more effectively than any shouting ever could.* Chairs clicking into place one by one *like dominoes falling.*

Waluigi has covered coups. Waluigi has covered the Regal Diet on a bad afternoon. Waluigi has watched men with titles and swords and standing armies fail to do what that girl did with one sentence, a hair-tuck, and a nod to three people she knew would move first. She has NO authority in that classroom. What she has is that everybody likes her and nobody wants to be the one person visibly ignoring her, and that is not a lesser form of power, it is the ACTUAL form, and the adult in the room had just spent two attempts demonstrating the inferior one.

What finally folded Lord Verity was a last warning — sit down or be removed. His fist was still up. The words died. The hoodie-cape slid off one shoulder and pooled on the desk behind him *like a deflated balloon,* and he said, in the best line of the entire morning:

**…You can't kick ME out. I'm not even IN anything yet.**

Then *fine,* through his teeth, and he sat. And the man thanked him for his cooperation with sarcasm the record measures as barely thin enough to pass through a colander.

Waluigi's finding for this section, stated flatly: the adult held the TITLE and the girl held the ROOM. Waluigi has seen that gap close badly in other institutions and Waluigi would like it noted early, while it is still funny.

sections.heading: He Could Have Let The Question Die And He Did Not
sections.body:
Now the part that turns an introductions session into a filing, and Waluigi wants to give the man his due before taking it back off him.

Seated at last, he leaned on the desk and started describing what the class IS. Students of Trinity General School. Here to learn, grow, be prepared for whatever comes next. Standard. Then: **SCHALE operations, academy life, the whole package.**

And from the floor, four syllables that Waluigi believes the man did not plan for: *SCHALE operations?*

Watch what that question does to the room, because the room answers it before he does. Lord Verity's eyes snapped to attention — real attention, the theatrical version gone in an instant, the pose melting *like frost in sunlight,* fingers tightening on the desk edge. **Wait. You're saying this class — THIS class — is connected to SCHALE? As in… actual missions? Real-world operations?** His voice cracked on *real-world.* And for exactly one second the record catches what is underneath the emperor act: *something raw — something hungry. Something that sounds like a kid who's been waiting for exactly this his entire life.* He started to say *I thought we were just—*, stopped, swallowed, and put the mask back on. The record says it no longer fit properly. WAH. Waluigi did not expect to be moved by the boy demanding that mortals kneel, and yet.

In the corner, Azusa's eyes sharpened — the record's image is *a blade being drawn from a sheath so smooth you'd miss it if you blinked* — and the name landed in her chest heavy and cold, because she already knows what systems that sort people into categories do to the people they sort. Yoshimi went shoulders-to-ears: *what does that have to do with ANY of us?* Hanae whispered the word to herself and got out **I… I know what that is** before her courage ran out at the two-second mark.

And then Shaggy said the thing.

**Like… okay, real talk. I've been at Trinity for a while now and nobody EVER explained this stuff to me. I get that there's Knights, I get that there's the Resistance, I even get that there's some kinda war going on — but 'operations?' Like… combat operations? Because if you're telling me I gotta fight something, I need to know where the nearest exit is first.**

Waluigi would like every institution in this archive to read that paragraph twice. A STUDENT of several years' standing, in good standing, enrolled, attending, has never had the organising structure of his own education explained to him. He knows there are Knights the way you know there is weather. He knows there is a war ON. NOBODY SAT HIM DOWN. And the only reason it came out at all is that a confused newcomer asked a question the returning students were too socialised to ask.

To his enormous credit — Waluigi is being sincere and it is costing him — the man put the clipboard down with a deliberate click, turned to face the room fully, held up a hand to stop Lord Verity interrupting, and answered.

**SCHALE isn't some secret club or a video game. It stands for Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution.**

Asked whether that sounded stupid, he said: **It does sound stupid. I'll give you that.** Waluigi nearly stood up and applauded. An adult, in front of children, conceding that his employer's name is nonsense. Then the recovery, and it is a good one: it is not an acronym people throw around for fun, it is the backbone of everything keeping the city breathing, it decides which Knights respond to hazards, how resources get allocated, WHO GETS SUPPORT WHEN THINGS GO SIDEWAYS.

Mari translated for everybody too embarrassed to ask, opening with the mercy line — *most people don't fully understand it until they're told directly* — and landing it in three sentences: the framework that keeps Kivotos stable, coordinating Knight response and Resistance intelligence, turning strategy into missions. *The difference between knowing there's a threat and actually doing something about it.*

Waluigi notes the mercy line especially. She did not say *you should know this.* She said MOST PEOPLE do not, which hands every embarrassed child in the room a way to keep their dignity while learning something. Waluigi has watched professional diplomats fumble that exact manoeuvre.

Then the whiteboard, and the geography: Sectors 7 through 12, eastern perimeter, warehouses, supply routes, abandoned industrial buildings that make excellent hiding places for people who do not wish to be found.

sections.heading: One Sentence, No Evidence, Eleven Children
sections.body:
He wrote **THE RESISTANCE** on the board in block capitals and underlined it twice, and then he said this:

**They're criminals who want to tear down everything Kivotos stands for — the academies, the peace agreements, all of it.**

Waluigi is going to slow all the way down, because this is the paragraph where an archivist either earns his keep or admits he is a fan.

That sentence is not a finding. It is a characterisation of an armed political faction, delivered in one line, without evidence, to a room of fourteen-year-olds, by a salaried employee of the body those people are fighting. Waluigi is not saying it is false. Waluigi genuinely does not know, and Waluigi wants to stress that he has no romantic attachment to insurgencies — he has covered enough of them to know how many are exactly what the state says they are. It may be true. It may be precisely and completely true.

What Waluigi knows is that NOT ONE PERSON IN THAT CLASSROOM HAD THE INFORMATION TO TEST IT. That is the FINDING. Eleven students, one of whom had just admitted nobody had ever explained the basic structure of their own institution to him, received the moral status of the enemy as a single declarative sentence and had no means whatsoever of checking it. They could not have pushed back if they wanted to. They did not have the facts. Nobody has ever given them the facts.

So the archive files it where it belongs: as the advisor's CHARACTERISATION, attributed to him, dated, in his words. Not as a fact about the Resistance. Waluigi has written *ask again in twenty sessions* into the event record and Waluigi means it as a standing instruction to himself.

And then he turned around and looked directly at the student who had asked, and gave the short version: **we're going there because someone's been moving weapons through those sectors, and SCHALE is the group that stops that from happening. You — all of you — are part of that.**

*You are part of that.* Waluigi wants to note the grammar. Not *you will be asked.* Not *you may volunteer.* You ARE. Past tense of a decision nobody in the room remembers making. Eleven children found out in the same sentence that they belong to an operational structure and that the operational structure has already assigned them a side.

Waluigi has a professional weakness for institutions that say the quiet part out loud, because they are so much easier to write about than the ones that do not. This one said it on a Tuesday morning before the deployment rotation had even been read out. Waluigi thanks him and files against him simultaneously, which is the job.

Two things sit underneath this that Waluigi refuses to let scroll past. The first is that the entire disclosure — the acronym, the function, the sectors, the enemy — happened because somebody confused asked an unembarrassed question. A more careful man lets that first *SCHALE operations?* die in the classroom noise. He genuinely could have. It would have cost him nothing and there was no one in that room positioned to press him. He answered instead, at length, and the archive got its first interior view of Kivotos as a direct consequence. Waluigi, grudgingly, on the record: that is better than the average.

The second is that the answering is exactly what produced the damage. He was honest about the acronym, honest that it sounds stupid, honest about the sectors, honest about the weapons intelligence — and in the same honest breath handed a room of minors a one-line verdict on a political movement, with the full authority of an adult at a whiteboard behind it. Waluigi has seen a great deal of lying in his career. Waluigi is increasingly convinced that candour without context does more work for an institution than lying ever did, because the children will remember that he told them the truth about everything else. That is the trap, and Waluigi does not think the man set it deliberately. Waluigi thinks he walked into it holding a marker.

sections.heading: A Diplomatic Programme, Discovered By Being Seen
sections.body:
Two more questions landed before the briefing could resume and both of them opened something the man would rather have kept shut.

The first arrived almost casually: what about the pony liaison from Equestria, some were seen walking around the school, was that meant to be private?

Waluigi enjoys this question enormously, and not only because the archive has a registered Equestrian lunar calendar sitting in its data files, quietly indexed to Canterlot and Ponyville, waiting since before anybody here needed it. Waluigi enjoys it because of what the man's FACE did. The record catches it: expression shifting, just barely, just enough for anyone paying attention. Jaw tightening a fraction. Clipboard set down with a deliberate click — the same click he used before answering the SCHALE question, which Waluigi now believes is his tell for *I am about to say something I will have to justify later.* And then words chosen like a man stepping over a tripwire he cannot see.

**That's… a separate matter.**

It was not a denial, and Waluigi wants credit given where it is due: he could have made it one. Instead he confirmed the thing. A diplomatic initiative between Kivotos and Canterlot. Small groups, cultural exchange, goodwill built in advance of the kind of mess that requires actual military coordination. *It was supposed to be handled quietly.*

Then the exhale through the nose, and the admission:

**So the fact that you saw them walking around openly tells me someone dropped the ball on security protocols somewhere along the line.**

Read that again with Waluigi. The failure he identifies is not that the programme is secret from the students. The failure is that the students SAW it. The problem is VISIBILITY. He then instructed the room to report further sightings *to me — not to social media, not to your friends, to me. Directly,* which converts eleven children into an informal counter-surveillance net against their own school's guests roughly ninety seconds after he told them they were part of SCHALE. Waluigi is not even angry. Waluigi is taking notes, because that was fast.

And in the corner, a pen stopped.

Azusa had two pieces that would not fit: an organisation that runs on need-to-know, and diplomatic personnel strolling a school corridor in plain view. She wrote something brief IN THE MARGIN that was NOT part of the lecture. She said **…Understood** to nobody in particular. She straightened a page that was already perfectly aligned, and resumed. Waluigi would pay money to read that margin. Waluigi suspects the archive will eventually have to.

Airi, meanwhile, had four questions and no filter: are there snacks in Sector 7, are the ponies friendly, can she hug one, and do they get breaks. Waluigi refuses to treat this as comic relief, because *do we get breaks* is a labour question and the child asked it inside a deployment briefing.

Then Shaggy made the structurally correct observation that nobody else made — if we're dealing with bad guys AND ponies showing up uninvited, that's two different problems, right? It IS two different problems. The advisor said so: the Resistance is an internal threat operating out of Kivotos, the liaisons are an external diplomatic situation *that someone mishandled,* his tone carrying an edge that suggested he has a name in mind and is not saying it. **The fact that those two things intersected at this school without proper coordination is exactly why SCHALE exists.**

Waluigi notes, because it is Waluigi's actual job to notice this, that the man twice attributed the failure to an unnamed *someone* who dropped a ball, and that the disappeared previous advisor of this same classroom also remains an unnamed someone. Two unexplained gaps at one school inside one hour, both routed into the passive voice.

On the hugging, he was unambiguous: they are not your friends, they are diplomatic personnel operating under an agreement *that does NOT include hugging.* Correct, joyless, and — Waluigi admits — the funniest sentence any adult produced all morning.

Waluigi is keeping a column for unnamed someones now. It has TWO entries and the morning was not yet over.

sections.heading: He Explained Need-To-Know Ninety Seconds After Breaking It
sections.body:
**We can all use guns at least right?**

Waluigi has read the transcript of the two seconds that followed this question several times and Waluigi maintains that they are the most interesting two seconds in the filing, because of who filled them.

Not the advisor. Kenzaki Tsurugi. The girl with her boots on the furniture, who had contributed one *keheh*, one *what a pain*, one *what a circus*, and nothing else all morning. She did not look at whoever asked. She kept her eyes on the adult. She uncrossed her arms slowly and deliberately, leaned forward, and pointed at him like a blade:

**…Seriously? If you're about to say 'yes' to that, then this class is just an excuse for a shooting range and I'm filing paperwork.**

And then: **I've handled weapons since before most of you were old enough to stop putting them in your mouths.** Arms recrossing with finality. **Sensei. What's the actual plan?**

Waluigi wishes to be extremely clear about what just happened, because the surface reading is *scary girl is scary* and the surface reading is WRONG. The most responsible position taken by any person in that classroom — adult included — was taken by the delinquent in the back row with her feet up, and she took it AGAINST her own evident interest. She is the one person present with weapons experience. A yes to that question would have made her the most important student in the room. She argued against it anyway, on the grounds that a class which arms children is not a class, and her threat was not violence, it was PAPERWORK. She threatened to FILE. Waluigi has never been prouder of anyone in this archive.

Shaggy got himself on the record immediately and defensively — wanted it noted that he said nothing about wanting guns, described himself and Scooby as diplomatic solution kind of guys, offered a bag of Scooby Snacks as his contribution to the mission. Waluigi accepts the contribution and has logged it.

The advisor exhaled slowly and delivered it flat: **Nobody is handing out guns.** Stone-cold finality. One second of silence. Correct answer, correctly given.

And then he ruined it.

He held up a finger to preempt an objection that Tsurugi had not made and showed no sign of making — she had just finished arguing HIS side — and added:

**—except Tsurugi. You already have clearance.** A beat. **Everyone else: no.**

Waluigi put the tape down and went for a walk.

She did not volunteer that. It is nowhere in the record that she offered it, hinted at it, or asked him to confirm it. He disclosed a student's weapons clearance to ten of her classmates, unprompted, in order to add emphasis to an argument he had already won by a mile. Everyone in that room now knows which one of them is armed. That is not a small fact to hand eleven teenagers about one of their own, and it is a fact she alone should have controlled the release of.

Then — THEN — he turned to the whiteboard and wrote **need-to-know** in block letters and underlined it twice, and explained that SCHALE tells you what you need for your assignment and you do not ask about things outside it. Anyone whose role requires a firearm will be briefed separately, with proper safety training, by certified personnel. *Not me. Not YouTube.*

Ninety seconds. Ninety seconds between broadcasting a thing nobody needed to know and underlining the principle that you are not told things you do not need to know. WAH. Waluigi could not have constructed a cleaner demonstration if he had been given a year and a budget.

The record does not show her reacting. No *keheh.* No *what a pain.* Nothing. Waluigi finds that the single most informative non-reaction of the morning, and Waluigi has written it into the event file in two separate places specifically so that it cannot be lost in the noise of the outfit committee that formed four minutes later.

Waluigi wants one more thing understood about her. She asked *what's the actual plan* and she never got one. The girl who argued against arming children, who threatened PAPERWORK rather than violence, who had the only relevant experience in the room — she asked the single most practical question of the session and the session moved on. Waluigi has now counted THREE unanswered questions and Waluigi is only writing down the ones that were said out loud.

sections.heading: Nobody Answered Her, And Then Nobody Answered Her Either
sections.body:
What this class did with a war briefing is form a committee about clothes, and Waluigi refuses to sneer at that, for reasons that will take a few hundred words to arrive at.

It started because he said there would be no cool gadgets and no matching outfits — *at least… not yet* — and let it hang. Amateur error. Airi nearly took out a juice box getting up: **WE'RE GETTING OUTFITS?!** What colour, what style, matching or pick-your-own, could hers have chocolate mint on it somehow. From the back, Tsurugi's mouth twitched: *…Not yet, huh. How long do we have to wait? …Days? Weeks?* Waluigi notes that the girl who wanted no guns wants the outfit and wants a DATE for it. Yoshimi's eye twitched and she announced she was opting out of group matching, last time the school made her wear anything she looked like a kid playing dress-up, and then exhaled through her nose like a frustrated bull at Airi's bouncing.

He tried to reclaim it. The outfits line was a joke. *Mostly.* SCHALE is not glamorous, it is paperwork and logistics and getting the right people to the right places when things go wrong. **But it IS important. The Resistance runs through this system. Every Knight deployment, every supply line, every evacuation order during a hazard event — it all flows through SCHALE.**

And from the corner, flat, like a weather report: **Cute outfits. …Who cares about outfits.** A shrug barely worth the name. And then the question this entire filing is built around:

**The question is whether SCHALE actually works. Or if it's just another thing that sounds important but doesn't do anything for people who are already at the bottom of every list.**

Then her gaze dropped to a closed notebook with a pen aligned parallel to its edge:

**…Doesn't matter though. I'm not on any list. Supplementary students don't count for much either way.**

NOBODY ANSWERED HER. Waluigi has checked the record four times. The lecture simply continued.

The committee formed anyway, around the newcomer's declared preference for cute clothes, and Waluigi is now going to defend it. Lord Verity rose to bless the arrangement, pivoted mid-sentence into *an alliance that shakes the very FOUNDATIONS of… SCHALE training readiness,* pointed at the advisor, retracted, pointed lower, and settled for nodding sagely. Yoshimi called it what it was — *they're forming an ALLIANCE over a cape* — declared she was not joining any alliance, and then in the very next breath said *but if Sensei needs someone who actually reads the handouts…* and slapped a crumpled pamphlet on the desk: **I finished page six.** She had been waiting the entire session for a reason to say that. Waluigi felt it in his chest.

Hanae raised her hand like she was asking permission at a town hall, offered logistics and scheduling, then produced a notebook of neat handwriting and colour-coded tabs: she had already organised the SCHALE information, *there were gaps in the documentation so I cross-referenced it with the school's emergency protocols.* NOBODY ASKED HER TO. It had been hours. She found GAPS. Waluigi would hire her tomorrow. Told *what no eww* in response to her paperwork offer, she should have folded — and instead lit up *like someone just turned on a lamp inside her chest cavity* and volunteered to check uniform modifications against school regulations. Airi called her a hidden treasure and shook her hands and she did not pull away. Then Airi proposed balloons on tactical gear, and got, from the back row, after a long stare: **…Keheh.**

Waluigi's point: an institution told these children they were part of an operation, declined to say what it was for, and the children immediately built the only structure in that room anybody chose. It has no remit. It is entirely THEIRS.

And then Mari raised a hand she did not need to raise and asked the last question:

**...whether SCHALE means we'll get to DO something meaningful. People don't care about gadgets or uniforms. They care about purpose. So… will it?**

The record does not show him answering. It shows him dropping into his chair like a man filling out paperwork about a natural disaster, and setting the order of business: deployment rotation first. Then fashion. The word came out *like he's chewing glass.*

Waluigi is going to drop the voice now, because the bit is not equal to this and pretending otherwise would be a kind of lying.

Two questions were asked in that classroom. A girl asked whether the system does anything for people at the bottom of every list, and told a full room that she is not on any list. Another asked whether any of it amounts to purpose. Both were AUDIBLE. Both were heard by eleven people and one adult. One received silence and the other received a deployment rotation.

Waluigi has spent this entire cut being funny about a classroom, and Waluigi would like the last two paragraphs read as though none of it were. An institution that will not answer *does this do anything for me* has answered. The archive will ask both again, in writing, every session, until somebody in that building says something. WAH.

commentaries.title: The Shepherd's Garden
commentaries.subtitle: In Which A Toad Catches A Boot, A King Passes A Test He Was Not Told He Was Taking, And Nine People Are Left In Crates
commentaries.filed: 3 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) — reconstructed from Bowser's retelling, which arrived quiet
commentaries.pullQuote: A shepherd tending a garden is a man who has confused two entire professions, and this is the being who claims to see the future.
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi was not in the Planar Sanctum, was not in the basement, and has had to assemble the most revealing hour of Bowser's life from a retelling that kept going quiet in the interesting places. This cut is also the first one where Waluigi went back through the rest of the archive line by line — and it changes the session. The Oracle's account of the assassination is corroborated in two places and contradicted in one. The Toad in the cellar was standing in the doorway when the cover-up was printed, eighty-five years ago. And the secret the satyr sells Bowser is something his own party generated at a map upstairs. There is still a boot.

sections.heading: Waluigi Watches A Toad Catch A Boot Out Of Nothing
sections.body:
Waluigi was not in the Planar Sanctum. Waluigi wants that established immediately, because what follows is the single most humiliating hour of Bowser's documented life and Waluigi did not get to watch ANY of it in person. Waluigi got it secondhand. Waluigi had to RECONSTRUCT it. This is the great tragedy of Waluigi's career: the best material always happens in rooms Waluigi has been excluded from.

So. Bowser is standing in a shattered star-lit library with a hole in the floor that he personally punched, and he opens with the obvious question. Why are you in this place.

And the Oracle says: **a shepherd needs to tend to his garden.**

Waluigi wants to stop here for a moment. A SHEPHERD. TENDS. HIS GARDEN. Waluigi has read that sentence eleven times and it gets worse every time, because shepherds do not have gardens. Shepherds have SHEEP. A shepherd tending a garden is a man who has confused two entire professions, and this is the being who claims to see the future.

Bowser — and Waluigi did not expect this — did not notice. Bowser instead said it reminded him of the galaxy, back when he took over the Mushroom Kingdom for a second. *For a second.* Waluigi enjoys that qualifier enormously. An entire kingdom conquest reduced to a scheduling footnote.

Then he noted the absences out loud. No stars. No Rosalina. And then, because Bowser's mind runs on rails and the rails only go to one place, he asked whether the Oracle had any stars.

The Oracle cast a fishing line into the void and pulled out a BOOT.

A boot. From nothing. In a dimension made of collapsed library and starfield, the custodian of the whole apparatus produced a rod, cast it into the abyss, and landed FOOTWEAR. Waluigi has no idea whether this was a joke, a trick, a demonstration, or genuinely the only thing down there, and here is Waluigi's favourite part of this entire filing: **neither does Bowser.** Nobody asked. The boot appeared, the boot hung in the air between them, and the conversation moved on as though a wet boot were a normal thing to pull out of the space between worlds.

Bowser's reaction was not anger. Waluigi wants to be precise, because this matters later: it was professional offence. *I'm the star of the show.*

And the Oracle told him he was relegated to the B plot.

WAH. WAH! A middle-aged Toad in robes, sitting on a floating slab of masonry, holding a boot, told the King of the Koopa Troop that he was a SUBPLOT. To his face. In his own scene. Waluigi has watched people lose fingers in this campaign for considerably less — Waluigi can name one — and this Toad delivered a structural critique of Bowser's narrative importance and then just kept fishing.

Bowser did not eat him. Waluigi cannot stress enough how strange that is. Hold that thought; the whole session is built on it.

One more thing about the boot, because Waluigi has decided it is load-bearing.

A boot is a JOKE. It is the oldest fishing joke there is — you cast a line, you reel in footwear, everybody laughs. But this Toad is not a comedian. This Toad is, by his own account minutes later, a man who warned a princess about her own assassination and watched her ignore him. So either the sanctum genuinely contains a boot, floating in the void between planes, for reasons nobody will ever explain — or a being who claims to see fate deliberately opened the most important conversation of the Raventree operation with a PUNCHLINE.

Waluigi thinks it was the punchline, and Waluigi thinks it was strategy. You cannot posture at a man who has just watched you pull a boot out of nothing. The boot lowered the temperature of the room. The boot made Bowser argue about BILLING instead of about leverage. And by the time anything serious was said, Bowser had already accepted the terms of a conversation in which he was the funny one.

That is not fishing. That is STAGECRAFT.

sections.heading: The Entire Conversation Was A Test And Nobody Told Him
sections.body:
Here is the thing Waluigi worked out only on the third pass through Bowser's retelling, and Waluigi is annoyed it took three.

There was never going to be a fight.

Go back and count what the Oracle did in that room. He insulted Bowser's importance. He barred him from the thing he wanted. He dangled a shortcut that was obviously poisoned. He brought up PEACH — the one subject in this entire archive that has reliably produced property damage, arson threats, and at least one destroyed hallway. He did all of it deliberately, in sequence, escalating.

And at the end he said so: *you've gotten soft. I insulted you, I barred you, I even mentioned Peach, and you didn't attack once.* Then — and this is the part Waluigi finds genuinely unpleasant — he added that half of what he said he did not mean, and hoped Bowser would not take it to heart.

**He was taking a reading.** The entire hour was instrumentation. Every provocation was a probe, and Bowser only found out he was being measured AFTER the measurement was complete and the number was written down.

Waluigi is going to drop the voice for a moment here, because the guide says to do it once per filing and this is the place.

That is a genuinely cruel thing to do to someone. Not the insults — Bowser has survived worse from Waluigi at a tennis match. The cruelty is the retroactive disclosure. You do not get to spend an hour pushing on a man's dead and then tell him it was a diagnostic. It converts his restraint, which was real and cost him something, into DATA. It takes the most difficult thing he did all night and files it as a test result.

Right. Voice back on.

Because Bowser's answer to all of this is the quietest line in his entire file, and Waluigi did not think this man had a quiet register. He looked DOWN — Bowser, looking down — and said that after what happened to Peach, he has not been the same.

And the Oracle said: *we all change, don't we. We just don't all reflect on our actions. Some change for the better, some for the worse.*

Waluigi has read that exchange perhaps twenty times now. Waluigi keeps expecting to find the joke in it. There is no joke in it. There is a very large lizard admitting grief to a small Toad who had just spent an hour poking him with a stick specifically to see whether the grief would come out as violence, and it did not, and the Toad wrote that down.

Bowser passed a test whose passing condition was NOT DOING ANYTHING. Waluigi would have failed it in under four minutes and Waluigi is aware of this.

Waluigi wants to add one structural observation, because Waluigi is the only person in this building who thinks about structure.

Look at the ORDER of the provocations. Importance first — you are the B plot. Then access — you are barred. Then temptation — here is a shortcut. Then, last, the dead. That is not a man losing his temper in escalating stages. That is a CHECKLIST, running from cheapest to most expensive, and the last item is the one that actually measures anything.

Insult a king's importance and you learn whether he is vain. Everybody already knew. Bar his path and you learn whether he is patient. Tempt him and you learn whether he is greedy.

Mention the woman he could not save, and you learn whether he is STILL DANGEROUS.

That was the real question. Everything before it was calibration — establishing a baseline so the final reading would mean something. And the answer the Oracle got was: no. Not in the way he used to be. Something in this man has been rerouted, and he now spends on thinking what he used to spend on arson.

Waluigi does not know whether the Oracle found that reassuring or disappointing. Waluigi suspects the Oracle found it USEFUL, which is worse than either.

### CROSS-REFERENCE: he always warns, and he always lets it happen

*I warned her* is not a new posture. It is this man's **documented operating procedure**, and the [Oracle's own dossier](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_oracle) has the receipts.

- He **warned an entire party about dimensional time dilation** while they were not listening. It happened anyway.
- He **warned the party that the Separation Ritual's mirror would interrogate their truths** — that a lie inside the circle would rupture it. Waluigi's note in that file, written long before tonight: *"Warnings can also be instructions for people paying close enough attention."*
- He **warned [Archie](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser) that he was absorbing too much power** during the transit ritual — and then allowed the ritual to proceed. Waluigi's filed hypothesis at the time was that this was a CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT.

So the pattern: state the danger accurately, on the record, then do nothing. Three times, documented, before Peach came up.

Which puts *I warned her, she ignored me* in an unpleasant light. It is technically true, it is exactly what he always does, and it discharges his responsibility perfectly. Waluigi would like to know what the warning actually SAID, because a warning delivered in the Oracle's usual register — oblique, unfalsifiable, structurally deniable — is not a warning. **It is an alibi you build in advance.**

sections.heading: The Oracle Has Been Spying On A Dead Woman And Says So Casually
sections.body:
Now the part Waluigi has been building toward, and Waluigi needs everyone reading this to sit down.

Bowser caught him. A snap of the fingers and a floating EYEBALL appeared — the Oracle had been using it to watch the Princess. Not metaphorically. A conjured eye, deployed over Princess Peach.

Bowser's objection was: *only I get to do that.*

WAH. Waluigi wants to award partial credit here. Bowser correctly identified that surveilling Peach is wrong. He then located the wrongness entirely in the question of LICENSING. It is not that someone is spying on her, it is that someone is spying on her WITHOUT BEING BOWSER. The man has built an entire moral framework and the only axiom in it is himself.

Then he declined to get angry at a little Toad, which is also new, and walked away.

But the Oracle kept talking, and this is where the session stops being funny.

Asked why he cared, he said he wanted to know what drives a person to kill someone. And then he described the room.

**Five or six mages' locks broken. The room untouched. She sat there with a comb in her hand, dead, unmoving, the blood staining the floor. The guards came in. They all died, and the record does not say why.**

Waluigi is going to go through that slowly, because Waluigi has been assembling the assassination file for a long time and this is the first eyewitness description of the scene the archive has ever held.

Five or six mages' locks BROKEN — so someone defeated serious warding, and defeated it loudly enough to leave the breakage visible. The room UNTOUCHED — so after defeating the warding, nothing was searched, nothing was ransacked, nothing was taken. A comb STILL IN HER HAND — she was not fighting. She was not fleeing. She was doing her hair. And then the responding guards, the ones who came in AFTERWARDS, all died, of causes nobody has written down anywhere.

Waluigi has filed a lot of murders. Murders are messy. Murders have overturned furniture and defensive wounds and a thief's logic you can follow. This is not a murder scene. **This is a composition.** Somebody broke in through heavy magic, killed a woman who was not resisting, touched nothing else, killed everyone who arrived to help, and left the tableau arranged for whoever opened the door next.

And then the Oracle said the sentence that Waluigi is going to be chewing on for months:

> *Yes. I know a lot of things. I ponder. I am the Oracle. I warned her. She ignored me — or maybe she didn't want to listen. She knew. She wanted to die.*

**HE WARNED HER.** He warned her and she did not act and he has been carrying that for eighty-five years and he told it to BOWSER, in a broken library, because Bowser had just finished proving he could be trusted not to swing.

Or — and Waluigi wants this flag planted right here, before anybody gets comfortable — **he says he warned her.** Nobody in that room could check. Nobody in that room was BORN. Waluigi has gone through the entire assassination file since, and what Waluigi found is in the next section, and it is not what Waluigi expected to find.

Bowser rejected it on the obvious ground — she had a kingdom to take care of, someone had to do it. And the Oracle killed the argument with one question: *was it really her kingdom, or the Mushroom Kingdom?*

Waluigi does not believe the Oracle is telling the truth. Waluigi believes he is telling A truth, carefully selected, released to a man he had spent an hour calibrating first. That is not the same thing and the archive should never confuse them.

And here is the question nobody in that room asked, which Waluigi will now ask on everyone's behalf:

**Why was the Oracle watching her AT ALL?**

Not eighty-five years ago. NOW. The eyeball was live. He conjured it in front of Bowser, which means it was a thing he does, not a thing he did once. Princess Peach has been dead since 955 BF. There is nothing left to surveil except a grave, an empty castle, and a Regency wearing her name like a coat.

So either he is watching the PLACE, which means he expects something there — or he is watching the FILE, which means somebody is still moving around her death, eighty-five years on, and he wants to know who.

Waluigi has a third possibility and Waluigi does not enjoy it: he is watching because he warned her, and she died anyway, and he has not been able to look away since. That is not intelligence work. That is GUILT with a magical apparatus attached to it.
